title: HOA backflow testing: create one asset and filing workflow
description: An HOA needs an association asset list, official notice owner, qualified tester path, access protocol, budget authority, and retained records.
prompt: How should an HOA turn annual testing into an owner-controlled asset process?
answer: An HOA needs an association asset list, official notice owner, qualified tester path, access protocol, budget authority, and retained records. A resident request alone does not establish the association compliance obligation.
urgency: Escalate unclear ownership, common-versus-private asset disputes, missing board authority, or an approaching deadline.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: Record whether the device serves common irrigation, a clubhouse, or another association system.
Identify who receives official notices and who approves service or repair.
Keep board-level records separate from vendor marketing or informal resident reports.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Map responsibility
steps.body: Confirm ownership and assembly inventory with the association record.

steps.title: Operate the workflow
steps.body: Schedule the required test with access and approval contacts named.

steps.title: Retain the proof
steps.body: Archive result, repair, retest, and filing evidence for the board record.

safeChecks: Verify asset identity and access responsibility before scheduling.
Use the official program requirement for tester and filing rules.
Keep the final record with the property or facility asset file.
stopConditions: Asset ownership or responsibility is disputed.
No official notice owner or repair authorization exists.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
evidenceNote: The official program controls testing and filing; exact manufacturer records control the identified assembly service path.
